questions.title: Average years of schooling among adults in Bangladesh
questions.hint: Each cohort of young people replaces an older one, so the adult average changes gradually.
questions.explanation: It rose to 6.8 years in 2023, from 3.8 years in 1995.

questions.title: Share of people with access to electricity in India
questions.hint: Connecting rural households is usually the slow part, and it depends on money and political priorities.
questions.explanation: It rose to 100% in 2023, from 51% in 1995.

questions.title: Average income (GDP per person) in Turkey
questions.hint: Economies grow in percentage terms, so the same growth rate adds more dollars each year.
questions.explanation: It rose to $35,069 in 2023, from $13,099 in 1995.

questions.title: Average number of children per woman in China
questions.hint: China’s one-child policy began around 1980 and was relaxed from 2016.
questions.explanation: It fell to 1.0 in 2022, from 2.7 in 1980.

source.attribution: UN Population Division, World Population Prospects

questions.title: People killed on the roads in Japan
questions.hint: Japan’s postwar car boom, a national campaign against the ‘traffic war’, a second wave of young drivers in the bubble years, then an ageing, safer country.
questions.explanation: It went from 12,055 in 1960 to a high of 16,765 in 1970, then ended at 2,839 in 2020. Deaths peaked at 16,765 in 1970, the height of what Japan called the ‘traffic war’. Sidewalks, guard rails, crossings and a 1970 traffic-safety law halved the toll by 1979, but it climbed back to 11,452 in 1992 before falling for three decades. Counts deaths within 24 hours of a crash.

source.attribution: Cabinet Office of Japan, Traffic Safety White Paper
